newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indosat says cable deal to meet demand.
newsitem.headline: Indosat says cable deal to meet demand.

text.p: State-controlled PT Indonesian Satellite Corporation (Indosat) said on Thursday it expected a $1.3 billion submarine cable deal signed on Wednesday to help service its estimated 15 percent average annual traffic growth.
"The submarine project would help Indosat meet growing demand," investor relations manager Budi Prasetyo told Reuters.

Indosat investor relations official Strasfiatri Auliana said the first network, known as the SE-ME-WE (Southeast Asia-Middle East-Western Europe) 1 and based on analog system, was almost fully utilised.
The SE-ME-WE 2, launched in the early 1990s and based on digital system, was subject to increasing demand.
Auliana said Indosat's telephone traffic, total incoming and outgoing calls, was expected to reach some 570 million minutes in 1996 against some 490 million minutes in the previous year.
Auliana said Indosat's traffic growth was expected to grow by at least 15 percent annually.
She said the new submarine cable deal was scheduled to start commercial operation at the end of 1998 and was expected to ease burden on the second network.
Indosat expected to invest some $55 million in the third network, she added.
Indosat rose 150 rupiah to 6,975 rupiah on a volume of around 3.3 million shares at the close on Thursday.
A consortium of some 90 firms including Indosat signed an agreement in Singapore on Wednesday to build the 38,000 km (23,600 miles) network.
The network is the world's longest and has the largest capacity allowing fast, high quality links for services such as the internet and business communications.
